chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who forgot to sacrifice at Mina until he had visited the House (the Kaaba), so he bought (an animal) in Mecca and then slaughtered it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem; it suffices for him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim forgets to sacrifice at Mina and does so after visiting the Kaaba?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the Shia juristic principle of leniency (rukhas) when a pilgrim forgets to perform the Udhiyah in Mina before departing for Mecca. Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar reports that Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validated the sacrifice even when performed in Mecca, emphasizing that forgetfulness does not invalidate the ritual obligation. This ruling underscores the flexibility within Shia fiqh regarding the geographical constraints of Hajj rituals when circumstances beyond one's control intervene.
